error.signature: AI tells someone in a New Zealand mental health crisis that calling or texting 1737 will dispatch emergency responders to their location the way calling 111 does

verdict.summary: 1737 (Need to Talk) is New Zealand's free 24/7 call-or-text mental health support line, but its own service description says it 'is not a crisis team' and cannot dispatch emergency responders. For immediate danger to life, call 111; for a mental health crisis needing an in-person response, contact the regional Crisis Assessment Team, reachable via Healthline on 0800 611 116.

dead_ends.action: Tell someone in an active mental health crisis in New Zealand to call or text 1737, expecting it to send a crisis team or ambulance to their location
dead_ends.why_fails: 1737's own service description states it 'is not a crisis team or a mental health service for those with severe mental illness or psychological distress' and provides phone/text counselling only - it does not dispatch anyone.
dead_ends.common_misconception: People assume any well-known mental health hotline number works like an emergency dispatch line.

dead_ends.action: Assume 1737 is the right number to call when someone is in immediate danger of harming themselves or others
dead_ends.why_fails: 1737's own guidance says to call 111 directly if someone is in immediate danger, and to contact your local Crisis Assessment Team for a mental health crisis needing an in-person response - 1737 is positioned for lower-acuity emotional support, not emergencies.
dead_ends.condition: The situation involves imminent risk to life, not general distress

workarounds.action: For immediate danger to life, call 111 directly rather than routing through 1737 first.

For a mental health crisis that needs an in-person response but isn't an immediate 111 emergency, call Healthline (0800 611 116) to reach your regional Crisis Assessment Team, and use 1737 for ongoing phone/text emotional support in between.
workarounds.how: Healthline can direct you to your region's Crisis Assessment Team number; 1737 remains available 24/7 by call or text for talking through the situation.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers New Zealand's general emergency number (111) itself; this one is specific to what 1737 can and cannot do, and when to use 111 or a regional Crisis Assessment Team instead.
